record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: How should nuclear-structure and isospin-breaking corrections to the Gamow-Teller-to-Fermi mixing ratio rho be computed for mirror beta decays, rather than assuming that the corrected rho entering the integrated decay-rate formula is the same effective rho extracted from angular-correlation measurements?

evidence.quote: Despite the potential for mirror decays in extracting competitive determinations of Vud, the evaluation of nuclear structure and isospin breaking corrections to the Gamow-Teller to Fermi mixing ratio has not been studied in detail.

where ρ is assumed to be the same as that obtained from measurements of angular correlation coefficients (see Sec. 3). As the Gamow-Teller matrix element can not be determined from first principles to a sufficient precision, this approximation is typically not given much attention.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an allowed nuclear beta decay between mirror nuclei (isospin doublet, T = 1/2). The decay rate has both a vector (Fermi) and an axial-vector (Gamow-Teller) contribution, parametrized by the Fermi matrix element M_F and the Gamow-Teller matrix element M_GT. Define the mixing ratio

  ρ = (C_A M_GT) / (C_V M_F),

where C_V and C_A are the vector and axial-vector coupling constants. The integrated decay rate (used in extractions of the CKM matrix element V_ud from mirror transitions) depends on a "corrected" mixing ratio ρ_corr that should incorporate nuclear-structure and isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections (analogous to the δ_C and δ_NS corrections in superallowed 0+ → 0+ Fermi transitions). On the other hand, angular-correlation observables (such as the β–ν angular correlation coefficient a_βν) yield an experimentally extracted effective ratio ρ_exp.

Provide a first-principles or systematic theoretical framework for computing the nuclear-structure and isospin-breaking corrections that relate ρ_corr to the bare ρ, and quantify the difference ρ_corr − ρ_exp for T = 1/2 mirror beta decays. In particular, determine to what extent the approximation ρ_corr = ρ_exp, commonly assumed in the integrated decay-rate formula for mirror transitions, is justified, and compute the leading corrections that must be applied to ρ_exp before its use in V_ud extractions.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent shell-model and configuration-interaction studies (e.g., 2022–2024) have begun computing isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections δ_C for T = 1/2 mirror Gamow-Teller transitions and explaining mirror asymmetries, but a systematic, first-principles treatment of the structure-dependent and isospin-breaking corrections to the mixing ratio ρ entering mirror-decay V_ud extractions—distinguishing ρ_corr from the angular-correlation ρ_exp—remains incomplete. The problem appears open, with active partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Shell-Model Description of the Isospin-Symmetry-Breaking Correction to Gamow-Teller β-Decay Rates and Their Mirror Asymmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Separates δ_C into δ_C1 (isospin mixing) and δ_C2 (radial mismatch) for Gamow-Teller transitions, noting first-order dependence absent in Fermi transitions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent shell-model work provides partial progress on isospin-breaking corrections to GT matrix elements in mirror decays.

status_evidence.title: Precision calculation of isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections to T = 1/2 mirror decays using configuration-interaction framework
status_evidence.snippet: Configuration-interaction framework built upon multireference charge-dependent DFT applied to T=1/2 mirror decays.
status_evidence.claim: Active research is computing isospin-breaking corrections for mirror decays, but a full treatment of ρ corrections is still developing.

status_evidence.title: Large mirror asymmetry in Gamow-Teller β-decay in the A=26 isobaric multiplet
status_evidence.snippet: Large mirror asymmetries in GT decays modeled via isospin-nonconserving shell-model interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Evidence that nuclear-structure-dependent corrections to GT matrix elements (and hence ρ) can be sizable and remain under study.
